name: dense_interval_residue
fixed_mission: unchanged; arbitrary public unmodified HF dense 405B, 8GiB, original outputs/RNG/successor state and same machine native4B Q4 ratios; no target claims
primary_question: Can dense (not sparse-support) exact corrections be sourced by few residue bits without reading all residual information?
comparison: A: interval-plus-residue lifting: no assumption of sparse output error
B: carry congruence state through nonlinear body, avoiding intermediate reconstruction
C: use joint vector syndromes rather than one remainder per coordinate
core_gate: construction, stored information, per-query source, state and native arithmetic must have a credible >=10x whole-body path; fail before large backend
classification: bounded auxiliary only if gate fails; THREE_QUALIFYING_NEW_PRINCIPLES=false until three qualifying constructions actually exist
exact_abi: finite integer BF16 weights, integer ternary inputs, every row has a positive coefficient, separate FP32 products balanced sum then BF16 RNE; declared absolute sum bound <2^24; no FTZ/reference CUDA assumption
preparation: choose median per row as cheap base; store min signed bit planes of residual, row L1 bound, and coarse base; no oracle, no unseen output lookup
queries: bits from current x select pos/neg masks. Generate each residue from serialized planes then interval lift. Exact row sums derived independently. Runtime not given original W. Compare to signed-bitpacked original, not only BF16.
prohibitions: do not equate less coefficient bytes with latency speedup
do not say modular integer equality implies arbitrary native BF16 equality
do not promote synthetic row residual regularity to arbitrary checkpoint
include header/row metadata, preparation pass, workspace, input parsing, each residue operation; hardware traffic/latency NOT_TESTED
scope_checks: nonlinear states same residue but different future
vector syndrome collision when decoder only receives syndrome and fixed side info
reproducibility: preregister hashes before running fixtures; deterministic results JSON and input hashes; unit tests, C or independent native reference; raw fixtures/output retained
